_disclaimer: Curated fixtures for the SigmaFold prototype. Every entry is either (a) public reference knowledge about a human gene, used as a teaching example, or (b) explicitly synthetic and labelled as such. No real patient data. No construct designs, guides, primers, vectors or protocols appear anywhere in this file, by policy (see SPEC.md section 7). Structural and simulation annotations are illustrative teaching summaries, not predictions from a validated model.

loci.name: Haemoglobin subunit beta
loci.note: The worked example for this prototype. The full reference coding sequence is included: 147 codons plus the terminator, taken from the NCBI reference record NM_000518.5 (see src/data/genomes/hbb-nm_000518.5.json for the retrieval provenance). This is standard textbook reference material. The first 31 codons translate to MVHLTPEEKSAVTALWGKVNVDEVGGEALGR; the full CDS translates to the 147-residue beta-globin chain.

cdsReference.label: HbA (reference allele)
cdsReference.note: Codon 148 is the terminator, so 147 codons encode residues. Sliced from the committed NM_000518.5 mRNA at 0-based offset 50; a test asserts this slice still matches that file.

exons.label: Exon 1
exons.note: Exon 1 encodes codons 1-30 plus the first base of codon 31, so codon 31 straddles the exon 1 / exon 2 boundary.

exons.label: Exon 2
exons.note: Codons 31-104, picking up from the second base of codon 31 and running into the first base of codon 105.

exons.label: Exon 3
exons.note: Codons 105-147 plus the terminator, picking up from the second base of codon 105. Ends the coding sequence.

variants.label: HbS (sickle allele)
variants.numberingNote: Codon 7 in CDS numbering. The legacy 'Glu6Val' name counts from the mature protein, after the initiator methionine is removed. Both names describe the same substitution.

structural.summary: A negatively charged, hydrophilic surface residue is replaced by a small hydrophobic one.
structural.consequence: The substituted hydrophobic residue sits on the surface of the beta-globin subunit. On deoxygenation this creates a sticky patch that favours contact between haemoglobin molecules, so they associate into fibres instead of staying in solution. Fibre formation is what stiffens and deforms the red cell.
structural.limitation: A qualitative teaching summary of a well-documented mechanism. Not output from a structure-prediction model.

variants.label: Repaired to reference codon
variants.numberingNote: The reverse substitution, restoring the reference codon at position 7.

structural.summary: Restores the reference charged surface residue.
structural.consequence: With the reference residue restored, the hydrophobic surface patch is gone and the deoxygenated protein no longer favours fibre formation, so cell shape is retained as oxygen tension falls.
structural.limitation: Models the sequence-level consequence only. Says nothing about whether any particular editing approach would achieve this in a cell, which is out of scope for this tool.

variants.label: Synthetic silent variant
variants.numberingNote: Invented fixture. Both codons encode threonine, so this exercises the diff view's 'silent' case — DNA changes, amino acid does not.

structural.consequence: No predicted change to the protein in this model.
structural.limitation: Entirely synthetic, included to test the diff renderer.

simulation._note: Parameters for the illustrative particle model in src/lib/cellsim. Chosen so the demo reads clearly on screen; they are not calibrated against experimental haemorheology data and must be presented in the UI as illustrative.
